title: Button stuck or pressed too long
causes: A control button has been held down for too long.
Moisture or grease on the control panel.
steps: Wipe the buttons with a damp cloth and dry the panel.
Check that no water is on or around the controls.
Switch the oven off, then try again.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Safety switch-off after long use
causes: The oven ran at one temperature for too many hours, so it shut itself off for safety.
This is not a fault.
steps: Switch the oven off.
Take the food out.
Start a normal cooking cycle again.
technician: No service needed unless it appears after a short cooking time.

title: Divider fitted wrongly for cook mode
causes: The divider was taken out during dual cook mode.
Or the divider was put in during single cook mode.
steps: Fit the divider for dual cook and remove it for single cook.
Switch the oven off and restart it.
If it persists, cut the power for 30 seconds or more, then restore it.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Divider fitted wrongly for cook mode
causes: The divider was taken out during dual cook mode.
Or it was inserted while using single cook mode.
steps: Keep the divider in for dual cook and remove it for single cook.
Switch the oven off and restart.
If it persists, switch off the breaker for 30 seconds or more and reconnect.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Door lock fault
causes: The oven detects a problem with the door lock.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
Do not force the door open if it is locked.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Oven sensor fault
causes: The oven reports a problem with a temperature sensor.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Oven sensor fault
causes: The oven reports a problem with a temperature sensor.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Oven sensor fault
causes: The oven reports a problem with a temperature sensor.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Memory read or write error
causes: An error happened while the control board read or wrote its memory (EEPROM).
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Main and sub boards not communicating
causes: The main circuit board and the sub board cannot talk to each other.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Touch controller communication problem
causes: The touch controller keeps losing contact with the main or sub board.
steps: Switch the oven off and start it again.
If the code stays, cut the power at the breaker for at least 30 seconds, then switch it back on.
technician: Call Samsung service if the code comes back after a full power reset.

title: Oven is preheating, normal message
causes: The oven is still heating up to the set temperature.
This is a normal message, not a fault.
steps: Keep the door closed.
Wait for the oven to reach the set temperature.
The code clears by itself.
technician: No service needed.

title: A control button is stuck
causes: A button was pressed for too long or has jammed.
Dirt or moisture around a button.
steps: Press each button one at a time and check it moves freely.
Clean the control area and dry it.
Switch the oven off and on again.
technician: Call Bosch service if E011 stays after cleaning the controls.

title: Oven cavity too hot, door locked
causes: The inside of the oven is too hot, so the door lock stays closed.
steps: Wait until the oven has cooled down.
Clear the message with the 0 button.
Do not force the door.
technician: Call Bosch service if E115 keeps returning when the oven is cold.

title: Control and power board not communicating
causes: The control panel and the power board lost their link.
steps: Switch the range off at the circuit breaker.
Wait five minutes, then switch the breaker back on.
Check whether the code returns.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Electronics fault
causes: The oven has detected an electronics fault.
steps: Switch the range off at the circuit breaker.
Wait five minutes, then switch the breaker back on.
Test the oven again.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Oven temperature sensor fault
causes: The temperature sensor is not working as expected.
steps: Switch the range off at the circuit breaker.
Wait five minutes, then switch the breaker back on.
If the oven was just installed, ask the installer to check the power cord wiring.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Oven door lock fault
causes: The door lock is not working correctly, often seen during self clean.
steps: Cancel the self clean cycle.
Wait for the door to unlock.
Start self clean again.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Control panel overheated
causes: The control panel is too hot, which pots on the cooktop can cause.
High room temperature.
steps: Check the room temperature and where pots are placed.
Let the appliance cool down.
Do a five-minute power reset at the breaker.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Power supply fault
causes: The supply voltage may be wrong or unstable.
steps: Switch the range off at the circuit breaker.
Wait five minutes, then switch the breaker back on.
Ask an electrician to confirm your home voltage if it returns.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Cooktop used during self clean
causes: A cooking zone was switched on while the oven was self cleaning.
steps: Turn off any active cooking zone.
Restart the self clean cycle.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: No service needed unless it appears with all zones off.

title: Demo mode is on, zones do not heat
causes: Demo mode is active, so cooking zones stay cold.
steps: Switch off the cooktop's breaker or fuse for 30 seconds.
Switch it back on.
Touch any control within three minutes.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Cooking zone overheated and shut off
causes: A zone overheated and switched off to protect the worktop.
steps: Let the electronics cool down.
Switch the zone on again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Cooking zone overheated and shut off
causes: A zone overheated and switched off to protect the worktop.
steps: Let the electronics cool down.
Switch the zone on again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Electronics overheated, zone off
causes: The electronics are too hot, so the zone switched off.
steps: Let the cooktop cool.
Touch any control.
Cook again once the message clears.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Electronics overheated
causes: The electronics are too hot.
steps: Let the cooktop cool.
Touch any control.
Resume cooking once the message clears.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Hot pan near the control panel
causes: Hot cookware is close to the touch controls.
The electronics risk overheating.
steps: Move the cookware away from the control panel.
Wait a few seconds and touch any control.
Resume cooking when the message clears.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Zone ran too long, time limit reached
causes: A zone was left on without any input for a long time.
steps: Touch any control.
Set the zone again.
Continue cooking.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Cooktop cannot connect to network or hood
causes: The cooktop lost its link to your home network or extractor hood.
steps: Switch the cooktop off and on.
Check your Wi-Fi is working.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the code returns after a power reset.

title: Supply voltage outside normal range
causes: The electricity supply voltage is too high or too low.
steps: Switch the cooktop off and on again.
Ask your electricity provider to check the supply voltage.
technician: Call Bosch support if your supplier finds nothing wrong.

title: Supply voltage outside normal range
causes: The electricity supply voltage is too high or too low.
steps: Switch the cooktop off and on again.
Ask your electricity provider to check the supply voltage.
technician: Call Bosch support if your supplier finds nothing wrong.

title: Cooktop not connected properly
causes: The wiring does not match the circuit diagram.
steps: Switch off the power at the breaker.
Have a qualified electrician check the wiring against the diagram.
technician: Call a qualified electrician or Bosch support.

title: Supply voltage outside normal range
causes: The supply voltage is outside normal limits.
steps: Switch the cooktop off and on again.
Contact your electricity provider to check the voltage.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Bosch support if the supply tests normal.

title: Electronics fault message
causes: The oven electronics have detected a fault.
It may be a one-off glitch.
steps: Switch the oven off and on again.
If the message disappears, it was a one-off.
If it returns, write down the exact code.
technician: Call Siemens after-sales service with the exact code if it returns.

title: Button permanently assigned
causes: A button is permanently pressed or assigned.
steps: Cancel the permanent button assignment.
Then press the clock function button.
Clean around the buttons.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Neff service if E011 does not clear.

title: Internal electronics fault
causes: An internal fault in the oven electronics.
steps: Press the clock function button.
If it stays, unplug the oven.
Wait about 10 seconds and plug in again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Neff service if the code returns.

title: Power was cut during operation
causes: The power supply was interrupted while the oven was running.
steps: Press the time of day button.
Reset the clock.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: No service needed unless it repeats without a power cut.

title: Descaling programme progress codes
causes: These codes show which step of the descaling programme is running.
E0 is drawing in solution, E1 activation, E2 to E4 rinses, E5 evaporating.
steps: Let the programme run to the end.
Do not switch the oven off during descaling.
technician: No service needed unless the programme stops.

title: Pyrolytic clean could not reach temperature
causes: The oven could not get hot enough for self cleaning.
A lot of food residue is inside.
steps: Switch the oven off.
Wipe out large deposits and heavy grime.
Start pyrolytic cleaning again.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Pyrolytic door lock does not close
causes: The self clean door lock is not engaging.
Something may block the door.
steps: Check the door and seal area for objects or debris.
Switch the oven off.
Start pyrolytic cleaning again.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Pyrolytic door lock will not open
causes: The self clean door lock has not released.
steps: Switch the oven off to stop the cleaning cycle.
Try opening the door.
Do not force it.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call Miele Customer Service if the door stays locked.

title: Electronic module fault
causes: The oven's electronic module has a technical fault.
steps: Do not try to repair it yourself.
Note the code and your model number.
Book a repair.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a Miele technician, as this cannot be fixed at home.

title: Technical fault detected
causes: The oven has detected a technical fault.
steps: Switch off at the breaker or unplug the oven.
Leave it off for 20 seconds.
Restore power and test.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Food probe is faulty
causes: The food probe or its connection is defective.
steps: Pull the probe out of its socket.
The fault message should clear.
Cook without the probe for now.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service to buy a replacement probe.

title: Oven switched off after running too long
causes: The oven ran for an unusually long time, so it shut off for safety.
The limit is 6 hours in grill modes and 12 hours otherwise.
steps: Switch the oven off, then on again.
Start a new cooking process.
technician: No service needed unless it keeps happening on short cooks.

title: Not enough oven ventilation
causes: The air duct is blocked or covered.
steps: Check that nothing covers the oven's air duct.
Disconnect the oven from power, then reconnect.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Oven cavity too hot
causes: The temperature sensor reports the cooking space is too hot.
steps: Switch the oven off and let it cool.
Do not try a repair yourself.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a Miele repair, as this needs a technician.

title: Demo mode on, oven does not heat
causes: Showroom demo mode is switched on.
steps: Confirm the message with OK.
Turn the mode selector to 0.
Open Settings, go to P 9 and set S 0.
Hold OK for 4 seconds.
technician: Contact Miele if demo mode returns.

title: Water container not pushed in
causes: The water container for pumping out leftover water is missing or not fully inserted.
steps: Push the water container fully into the oven.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Power cut during cooking
causes: The oven lost power during a cooking programme.
steps: Check how far cooking has got.
Set a new cooking time if needed.
Press Start/Stop to resume.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Water not reaching steam oven
causes: The water intake valve is not fully open.
The water nozzle is blocked with limescale.
steps: Open the water intake valve fully and restart.
Descale the water nozzle if it returns, using oven gloves.
Flush the water parts.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Water inlet fault in steam oven
causes: The feed pump is dry after long non-use.
The black suction hose is loose or damaged.
Osmosis water is too pure for the sensor.
steps: Refit the black suction hose upright in the container.
Switch off the osmosis system if you can.
Or add a pinch of salt to the water.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Steam generator cannot drain water
causes: Limescale in the drain or on the electrode.
Blocked or stuck hoses.
steps: Descale the oven as described in the manual.
Set water hardness to maximum on 6000 and 7000 series.
Do not repeat descaling with stronger solution.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Steam oven not receiving water
causes: The water intake valve is closed.
The water inlet filter is blocked.
steps: Open the water valve and restart.
Clean the filter in the water inlet.
Turn the oven off and shut the valve if you suspect a bad hose.
technician: Call Miele or a plumber if the hose looks faulty.

title: Steam oven compartment too hot
causes: The water intake valve may be closed.
The water nozzle may need descaling.
steps: Open the water intake valve fully.
Descale and rinse the nozzle if it returns.
Wear oven gloves.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Not enough water in steam generator
causes: Not enough water is reaching the steam generator.
steps: Switch the oven off and on again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Switch off and contact Miele if F14 appears again.

title: Steam oven not heating
causes: The temperature did not rise 2 degrees in 5 minutes.
Large amounts of frozen food can cause this.
steps: Switch the oven off and on and restart.
Push the water container in until it clicks.
Use only the supplied silicone grease on the seal.
technician: Call Miele if the coupling seal looks cracked or water collects.

title: Power cut during cooking or descaling
causes: Power was cut during a cooking programme (F27).
E04 means power was cut during descaling.
steps: For F27 set a new time and press Start/Stop.
For E04 wait until the display counts down from 0:06.
Switch the oven off and on.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Technical fault in steam oven
causes: A technical fault that cannot be fixed at home.
steps: Do not try to repair it yourself.
Note the code and model number.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a Miele technician visit.

title: Water level switch blocked by limescale
causes: Limescale blocks the level switch.
steps: Descale the oven as in the manual.
Use Miele care products.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact Miele Customer Service or book a repair if the fault returns.

title: Electronic module fault
causes: The electronic module is faulty.
steps: Do not attempt a DIY fix.
Note the code.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a Miele repair.

title: Oven door cannot lock
causes: Pyrolytic models: the clean function is on and the door will not close.
Other models: an electronic fault.
steps: Check the upper door section is intact.
Follow the manual if the door was removed.
Contact service if it persists.
technician: Book an Electrolux repair if the code returns.

title: Door lock sensor fault
causes: The door is not fully closed.
A faulty door lock or electronics.
steps: Close the door firmly.
Cut power for a few minutes, then restore it.
Check the house fuse or RCD.
technician: Book an Electrolux repair if the code returns.

title: Food probe faulty or not connected
causes: The probe is not plugged in fully.
The probe or its cable is damaged.
steps: Unplug and reconnect the probe firmly.
Check for bent contacts or damaged wire.
Switch the oven off at the mains for 30 seconds.
technician: Book an Electrolux repair if the code returns.

title: Temperature sensor out of range
causes: The oven temperature sensor is out of range.
The oven may not heat or may stop.
steps: Switch the oven off at the mains for 30 seconds.
Switch it back on.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact an Authorised Service Centre.

title: Temperature sensor too-high alarm
causes: The sensor detected a temperature above the expected level.
steps: Switch the oven off and let it cool.
Switch off the power for 30 seconds, then restore.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact an Authorised Service Centre.

title: Connected oven software fault
causes: A software problem on a connected oven.
steps: Reinstall the app and reconnect the oven.
Unplug the oven for 30 minutes, then reconnect.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a repair if F215 shows on the display.

title: Oven Wi-Fi signal problem
causes: There is a problem with the Wi-Fi signal.
steps: Check your network connection.
Move the router closer.
Reset the oven Wi-Fi settings and set up again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a repair if it will not connect.

title: First Wi-Fi connection attempt failed
causes: The first attempt to connect to Wi-Fi failed.
steps: Power the oven off and on.
Try connecting again.
Check your internet connection.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book a repair if it will not connect.

title: Oven light not working
causes: The oven bulb is faulty.
steps: Switch the oven off and let it cool.
Check the bulb and replace it if faulty.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact a service centre if the bulb is fine.

title: Pyro clean blocked by telescopic rails
causes: Telescopic rails are in the oven.
steps: Remove rails, shelves and side runners.
Start Pyro Clean again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact service if it persists.

title: Pyro clean blocked by food probe
causes: The food probe is plugged in.
steps: Unplug the probe from its socket.
Start Pyro Clean again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact service if it persists.

title: Pyro clean blocked by open door
causes: The door is open or not fully closed.
steps: Close the door completely.
Start Pyro Clean again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact service if it persists.

title: Pyro clean blocked by Steam Bake
causes: Steam Bake is still active.
steps: Press Steam Bake until its light goes off.
Start Pyro Clean again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Contact service if it persists.

title: Cookware not detected or hob fault
causes: Unsuitable pan or pan lifted off.
On a new install, an installation problem.
steps: Check a magnet sticks to the pan base.
Centre the pan on the zone.
Keep hob and pan dry.
Switch off at the mains for 30 seconds.
technician: Book an engineer if F stays or has a digit.

title: SenseBoil: empty pot or oil
causes: The pot is empty or holds oil or a liquid other than water.
steps: Dry the hob surface.
Do not heat an empty pot.
Use SenseBoil with water only.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Not a fault if cleared.

title: SenseBoil: wrong amount of water
causes: Too much or too little water in the pot.
Food other than water or potatoes.
steps: Dry the hob surface.
Fill the pot half to three quarters, 1 to 5 litres.
Boil only water and potatoes.
technician: Not a fault if cleared.

title: Hob LED or sensor error
causes: On induction hobs an LED lighting error.
On teppanyaki a temperature sensor error.
steps: Cut the power for 30 seconds.
Switch back on.
Note the exact code.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob connected to wrong voltage
causes: Possible overvoltage or incorrect wiring.
steps: Stop using the hob.
Ask the installer to check supply and wiring.
Do not fix electrics yourself.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Call a qualified electrician or AEG service.

title: Hob overheating protection active
causes: The hob overheated.
Unsuitable cookware or poor installation.
steps: Switch off and remove cookware.
Test pan with a magnet.
Cut power for 30 seconds.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob phase or voltage problem
causes: A phase or voltage problem in the power supply.
steps: Switch off the isolating switch for 30 seconds.
Switch on and test.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob power supply problem
causes: Often incorrect installation, such as a 13 amp socket for a 16 amp hob.
steps: Switch the hob off and on.
Disconnect for 30 seconds.
Have the supply checked.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob cooling fan fault
causes: Fan blocked or faulty on newer models.
steps: Check nothing blocks the fan under the hob.
Cut power for 30 seconds.
Switch on again.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob electronics or phase fault
causes: A missing phase after installation.
Electronics communication error.
steps: Check wiring against the manual.
Cut power for 30 seconds.
Stop using it if it persists.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Hob electronic module fault
causes: A fault in the electronic module.
steps: Switch off at the mains for 30 seconds.
Do not use the hob if it returns.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Book an AEG repair if the code returns.

title: Oven control fault unidentified
causes: The control cannot identify the fault.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Possible sensor, control or wiring fault
causes: Oven temperature sensor, control or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Possible sensor, control or wiring fault
causes: Oven temperature sensor, control or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Keypad or control problem
causes: Keypad, control or wiring problem.
A grate may be seated badly.
steps: Check the grates sit level.
Swap them if they wobble.
Turn the breaker off for a minute.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Possible oven control or wiring fault
causes: Oven control or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Oven door latch problem
causes: Door latch, switch or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Oven door latch problem
causes: Door latch, switch or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Possible oven control or wiring fault
causes: Oven control or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Door latch assembly problem
causes: Door latch assembly or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Oven cooling fan running slowly
causes: Airflow restriction.
Faulty cooling fan or wiring.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Door latch or lock switch problem
causes: Door latch, lock switch or wiring problem.
steps: Switch off the range's circuit breaker for one minute.
Switch it back on.
Watch the oven for a minute to see if the code returns.
technician: Contact Whirlpool service if the code returns.

title: Upper oven thermistor error
causes: Upper oven temperature sensor fault.
steps: Press CLEAR/OFF and try the function again.
Turn off the range's breaker for 30 seconds.
Switch it back on.
Write down the exact code and the model number from the rating plate before you contact anyone.
technician: Request an LG repair if it keeps coming back.

title: Upper oven thermistor error
causes: Upper oven temperature sensor fault.
steps: Press CLEAR/OFF and try the function again.
